 ## Search results
NextItNet’s foundation is stacked causal dilated convolutions with residual blocks, expanding receptive fields to capture longer dependencies without pooling. The search did not establish a directly matching 2024–2026 NextItNet variant with learned gates over dilation scales. Related work supports individual ingredients: AFMN combines multiscale convolutions with frequency-aware attention for sequential recommendation; 2026 FAAM-SR uses frequency-aware gating to balance repetitive behavior and exploratory interests. These provide motivation, but do not demonstrate that gated dilation scales improve NextItNet. [NextItNet](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf), [AFMN](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.asoc.2022.109349), [FAAM-SR](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ins.2026.123580).

A relevant cross-domain architectural precedent is CVPR 2024’s Frequency-Adaptive Dilated Convolution, which adapts dilation and frequency selection for semantic segmentation; its results do not establish recommendation gains. An inferred experiment is to retain NextItNet residual blocks while introducing parallel causal convolution scales, such as dilations 1/2/4, and jointly learned, position-dependent softmax gates conditioned only on available history. Small receptive fields could emphasize recent intent while larger fields retain older context. Keep all branches inside one jointly trained network and checkpoint per category, mask padding, and read the final nonpadding position. Compare against fixed-scale and uniformly weighted variants using the pinned macro validation HR@10; stale-interest suppression remains a hypothesis requiring measurement. [FADC](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.05369).

Recent research supports text-enhanced sequential recommendation, but the retrieved 2024–2026 work does not establish an exact match for a jointly trained, randomly initialized text encoder inside NextItNet. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) combines item IDs with titles, descriptions and reviews, but uses pretrained BERT and a SASRec-based backbone; its strongest textual contribution comes from reviews, unavailable here. [DWSRec (2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28786) likewise depends on pretrained text embeddings, investigating their geometry rather than learning text features from scratch.

A compatible experimental hypothesis is to retain [NextItNet’s residual dilated convolutions](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163), adding a small, randomly initialized token encoder over available titles and descriptions. Mean-pooled token embeddings or a shallow text CNN could feed a learned projection and gate into each item representation, trained jointly with the next-item objective in one network. This is a proposed adaptation, not a demonstrated result from the retrieved papers. Preserve the ID pathway, handle missing text explicitly, and compare against the corrected baseline using macro validation HR@10.

Complementarity requires particular caution: [McAuley et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.08839) distinguish substitutes from complements through supervised product-link prediction, using reviews and additional metadata. Those labels and inputs are unavailable here. Titles and descriptions may help distinguish product purposes, while ordered interactions may teach useful transitions, but neither establishes compatibility, redundancy or purchase intent as observed ground truth. Treat these interpretations as hypotheses; avoid labeling similar products as substitutes or consecutive purchases as complements.
